analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/configuration.md adds one row at head line 669 for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS, which is default-on and negative values disable it. It says native recurrent complete checkpoints are written as deltas of the restored file, and that the setting is not forwarded to LaunchAgents. docs/developer/test.md only adds benchmark-report fields (delta files, greedy output tokens) and a baseline toggle. The supplied test.md excerpt (head lines 946-1326) does not show those lines, but the patch metadata covers them. No code or controls changed in the supplied evidence.

Threat relevance: T-041 (prefix-cache at-rest artifacts, A-001) and the TB-007 cache surface. The described delta-checkpoint feature adds a storage format, the dependency of a delta on its restored base file, and a default-on path. The provider code (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift, SSDBlockStore, and the rest) was not supplied, so these were not verified. Questions for the code-bearing review:
- Whether delta files keep HMAC-only names and AAD with no prompt-derived plaintext metadata.
- Whether deltas keep cacheSalt scoping, so entries cannot resolve across scopes.
- Whether a delta can name its base in plaintext in a way that leaks prefix identity.
- Whether TTL, LRU and KEK-wipe purge cover delta files and base-chain dependencies.
- Whether write-endurance accounting and rollback/replay binding of base to delta hold.
No concrete regression can be asserted from documentation alone. The docs claim nothing contradicting the T-041 mitigations. The threat model may need a note on delta artifacts once the implementation is reviewed.
